name: Four Seasons Hotel Boston
insider_take: Boston's most prestigious address sits where high society meets revolutionary history, overlooking the Public Garden where Make Way for Ducklings comes to life.
whats_special: This iconic hotel occupies prime real estate on Arlington Street, directly across from America's first public botanical garden. The property features one of Boston's most celebrated restaurants, and many rooms offer coveted views of the Swan Boats gliding through the lagoon that inspired Robert McCloskey's beloved children's tale.
pro_tip: Request a Public Garden view room on floors 8-15 for the best vantage point of the seasonal tulip displays and fall foliage that transforms the garden into a painter's palette.
dont_miss: Take the hotel's complimentary bikes for a sunrise ride along the Charles River Esplanade, or walk 3 minutes to feed the famous bronze ducklings statue - a Boston tradition that brings good luck to visitors.
pros: Prime location in Back Bay with easy access to shopping and attractions
Exceptional personalized service with attention to detail
Elegant rooms with high-end amenities and city views
cons: Urban setting lacks outdoor recreational spaces
